newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria rebels kill man, attack water supply - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algeria rebels kill man, attack water supply - paper.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed a shopkeeper in northeastern Algeria and blew up a water distribution network in a southern region, an Algerian newspaper said on Monday.

El Watan newspaper named the shopkeeper as Meziane Bourguiba, 40, and said he was killed on Saturday night at a fake roadblock put up by rebels in Ain el Hammam area, 90 km (56 miles) east of Algiers.
Two men travelling in the same car as the shopkeeper were able to drive off and escape, the newspaper said.

About 10 rebels at the weekend destroyed a water pumping stations in Djelfa region, about 230 km (143 miles) south of Algiers, blowing up part of it with explosives and machinegunning other equipment, cutting off water to residents, El Watan said.
Algerians in the country's main cities are struggling with water shortages caused by a serious drought this year which has forced the authorities to ration supplies.

President Liamine Zeroual vowed on Sunday that his government would implacably pursue Moslem rebels whom the authorities blame for a latest wave of massacres and bombings in which about 1,000 people have died in the past two months.
But the Algerian Liberte newspaper, while hailing Zeroual's commitment, said ordinary Algerians wanted to know the official assessment of the violence in the country.
Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour briefed Sunday's cabinet meeting on the security situation but no details were given in the official report of the session.
About 60,000 people have died in violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
